skill.name: observability-engineer
skill.description: Design production monitoring, logging, tracing, SLO, alerting, and incident response strategies for cloud, enterprise, and distributed systems.
skill.summary: Design reliable observability systems that connect telemetry, service objectives, alerts, dashboards, and incident workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by benign observability and access-control language. SKILL.md contains guidance only, with no commands, prompt injection, credential collection, or exfiltration intent.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid logging sensitive data or secrets.
- Multi-cloud and hybrid monitoring strategies across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-premises
- Active Directory and SAML integration for monitoring access

finding_verdicts.reason: The line explicitly advises users to avoid logging sensitive data or secrets. It is protective observability guidance, not system reconnaissance.
The line lists multi-cloud and hybrid monitoring as a knowledge area. It provides no host discovery, enumeration, or reconnaissance instructions.
The line describes Active Directory and SAML integration for authorized monitoring access. It contains no network scanning, discovery procedure, or executable command.

content.value_statement: Fragmented telemetry obscures service health and delays incident response. This skill designs metrics, logs, traces, SLOs, dashboards, alerts, and operational workflows.
actual_capabilities: Designs monitoring architectures for cloud, Kubernetes, microservice, serverless, and hybrid environments.
Defines SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, burn-rate alerts, and reliability reporting.
Plans metrics, structured logging, distributed tracing, sampling, retention, and telemetry correlation.
Creates dashboard, alert-routing, runbook, escalation, and post-incident analysis strategies.
Evaluates observability tools, costs, compliance requirements, access controls, and data residency.
Develops OpenTelemetry collection, processing, and multi-backend export designs.
limitations: Requires environment details, telemetry samples, reliability targets, and operational constraints for specific recommendations.
Does not directly deploy infrastructure, query live systems, or validate production behavior.
Cannot replace security, compliance, or legal review for regulated telemetry.
Recommendations require testing for scale, cost, signal quality, and alert noise.

use_cases.title: Define service reliability targets
use_cases.description: Convert critical user journeys into measurable SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, and burn-rate alerts.

use_cases.title: Investigate production regressions
use_cases.description: Correlate metrics, logs, and traces to isolate latency, availability, and dependency failures.

use_cases.title: Govern enterprise telemetry
use_cases.description: Plan retention, access controls, data residency, reporting, and monitoring costs across complex environments.

prompt_templates.title: Create a service monitoring plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an observability plan for [service]. Include critical user journeys, key metrics, dashboard sections, alert thresholds, and required context.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one service and its primary reliability needs.

prompt_templates.title: Define service objectives
prompt_templates.prompt: Define SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, and burn-rate alerts for [service] using these user journeys and reliability expectations: [details].
prompt_templates.scenario: Translate business expectations into measurable reliability targets.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this incident evidence: [metrics, logs, traces]. Identify likely causes, missing signals, validation steps, and an investigation sequence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Correlate available telemetry during a production regression.

prompt_templates.title: Design an enterprise telemetry platform
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-region OpenTelemetry architecture for [environment]. Address collection, sampling, routing, retention, data residency, failure handling, costs, rollout, and validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a governed observability platform across regions and providers.

output_examples.input: Create monitoring guidance for a customer checkout API.
output: An SLI set covering successful checkouts, latency, dependency errors, and payment outcomes.
A dashboard plan linking user impact, service health, dependencies, and deployment changes.
Burn-rate alerts with investigation steps, ownership, and escalation guidance.

output_examples.input: Plan tracing for a high-volume microservice platform.
output: An OpenTelemetry data flow from instrumentation through collectors to selected backends.
A sampling strategy that preserves errors and rare transactions while controlling cost.
A rollout plan covering validation, capacity, privacy, and failure handling.
An alert inventory grouped by user impact, urgency, ownership, and actionability.
Recommendations for deduplication, dependency-aware routing, threshold tuning, and removal.
Success measures covering page volume, false positives, response time, and missed incidents.

best_practices: Provide service architecture, user journeys, current telemetry, traffic patterns, and reliability targets.
Validate recommendations with production-like load, failure tests, and representative telemetry.
Review telemetry for secrets, personal data, retention obligations, and access-control requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not collect every available signal without a clear reliability or operational purpose.
Do not page responders for conditions without user impact, urgency, ownership, and a defined action.
Do not adopt generated configurations without environment-specific testing, capacity review, and rollback planning.

faq.question: Which observability tools does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Jaeger, Loki, ELK, Splunk, cloud monitoring services, and related enterprise tools.

faq.question: Can it define SLIs and SLOs?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide user journeys, service boundaries, reliability expectations, measurement windows, and available telemetry.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot a live incident?
faq.answer: It can analyze supplied evidence and propose investigation steps, but it cannot access or change live systems.

faq.question: Does it generate deployment-ready configurations?
faq.answer: It can propose configurations and architecture, but every output requires testing, security review, and environment-specific validation.

faq.question: Can it help control telemetry costs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can assess sampling, cardinality, retention, storage tiers, backend selection, and collection scope.

faq.question: Does it support regulated environments?
faq.answer: It considers access, retention, audit, residency, and privacy requirements, but qualified reviewers must confirm compliance.
